review_comments.body:
Usually the platform logs have color coding around them. This regexp does not handle that majority use-case. Also nested level redirects will probably not match.

This will always be a guessing. No way to make this 100% correct and not worth putting much effort into it as user can define their own logger.

So I would be in favor of keeping this as simple as possible.

Maybe small improvement and still simple enough would be printing the first matching level.

Something like

```
ANSI_CODE = re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m')
FIRST_WORD_PATTERN = re.compile(r'\b(CRITICAL|FATAL|ERROR|WARNING|WARN|INFO|DEBUG)\b')
LEVELS = logging.getLevelNamesMapping()

def guess_first_word(message: str) -> int:
    """First whole-word level name anywhere in the line, with ANSI color codes removed first."""
    match = FIRST_WORD_PATTERN.search(ANSI_CODE.sub('', message))
    return LEVELS[match[1]] if match else logging.INFO
```

We are on Python 3.11+

Can t we do just something as simple as 

```
try:
   await asyncio.wait_for(self._streaming_task, timeout=self._stop_timeout_s)
except (TimeoutError, asyncio.CancelledError):
   pass
```

comments.body:
Thanks @Pijukatel. I pushed e71c4f6 with the review applied: the level guess now strips ANSI codes and only looks at the first level, and the async stop wait is simplified to a plain `wait_for`. One addition: cancellation from the caller propagates through `cancelling()`, and a unit test covers it.
